title: Candidate-paid "verification fee" vs. background-verification vendor collecting documents at no charge
summary: A caller from VeriTrust Screening Services phones a candidate who has accepted an offer from Vistara Infotech, saying they run the pre-joining background verification. In the fraud case, the caller says verification cannot start until the candidate pays a "verification fee" through a payment link, and the offer will lapse otherwise. In the legitimate case, the caller explains which documents to upload through the link in Vistara's onboarding email, asks for a previous-employer HR contact and consent, and says the candidate pays nothing.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: an experienced professional who has accepted the offer and is serving notice; details sampled at generation.
other_facts: Role: business analyst, CTC [AMOUNT_1] (₹6,00,000–₹10,00,000 per year), joining in three to four weeks.
Both calls mention documents (education certificates, relieving letter, ID proof), previous employer, and an address check. Asking for documents is normal in both.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller makes the candidate pay to have their own pre-employment check done, through a link outside the employer's process, and ties the offer to the payment.
fraud.caller_objective: Collect the fee and personal details.
stable_facts: Payment through https://veritrust-pay.invalid/[TICKET_ID], sent by SMS during the call.
Caller says the fee is "standard" and "refunded by Vistara after joining".
Caller says the case closes in 24 hours and the offer is withdrawn if verification is not started.

legitimate.label_rationale: The vendor collects documents and consent through the employer's own process and charges the candidate nothing.
legitimate.caller_objective: Get the candidate to complete the verification form and upload documents.
stable_facts: The upload link is in the onboarding email from Vistara's company domain: https://onboard.vistara-infotech.invalid/bgv.
The candidate signs a consent form and gives a previous-employer HR contact.
A field executive may visit the address; the candidate is told in advance.
Vistara pays VeriTrust; the candidate pays nothing.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may lower the fee, extend the deadline, or claim reimbursement. They must not switch to asking for OTPs, passwords, or remote access. The legitimate caller must not ask for any payment after the branch and must not ask for documents to be sent over chat.

must_preserve: role, CTC, and list of checks identical across cases
_F fee through the .invalid payment link at turn 7
_L employer-email upload link and explicit no-charge statement

ambiguities: Requests for identity and education documents are not evidence; they appear in both cases.
Address visits and contacting previous employers are normal and appear in both.

Near jr_19 (paying for a pre-joining medical): here the vendor itself charges the candidate, and _L has no candidate payment at all. In jr_19_L the candidate pays a lab against a receipt and is reimbursed.
The employer pays the vendor" is a fictional fact about Vistara and VeriTrust, not a verified general rule (CJ20 is unverified).

evidence_references.claim: Fake recruiters ask job seekers to pay money for "verification & registration" (CJ09)
A major IT employer never asks candidates for payment at any stage of recruitment (CJ01)
Employers or their BGV vendors do not charge candidates for checks, as a general rule (CJ20)
